title: Death as a Wedding — Rumi's Shab-e Arus
subtitle: Eight Persian Sufi poems with English translation
yt_title: Death as a Wedding — Rumi's Shab-e Arus | 8 Persian Sufi Poems (English Translation)
intro: Rumi died in Konya on the seventeenth of December, 1273.
His followers do not call that night a funeral. They call it Shab-e Arus: the wedding night, the night the soul meets its Beloved.
Here are eight passages in which Rumi speaks of death without fear.

poems.name: On the Day of My Death

lines.fa: به روز مرگ چو تابوت من روان باشد
lines.en: On the day of my death, when my coffin is moving,

lines.fa: گمان مبر که مرا درد این جهان باشد
lines.en: do not imagine that I feel pain for this world.

tafsir: This is perhaps Rumi's most famous poem about his own death.
He imagines his coffin carried through the streets.
And he turns to the mourners: do not think I am sad to leave.
For him, the coffin is not a prison. It is a carriage to a wedding.

poems.name: The Human Seed

lines.fa: کدام دانه فرورفت در زمین که نرست
lines.en: Which seed ever went down into the earth and did not grow?

lines.fa: چرا به دانهٔ انسانت این گمان باشد
lines.en: Why do you have this doubt about the human seed?

tafsir: From the same ghazal comes this simple, powerful question.
Every farmer buries seeds and waits for them to rise.
No one weeps over a planted seed.
Rumi asks: why should a human being be the only seed that does not grow?

poems.name: Die in This Love

lines.fa: بمیرید بمیرید در این عشق بمیرید
lines.en: Die, die, die in this love;

lines.fa: در این عشق چو مردید همه روح پذیرید
lines.en: when you have died in this love, you will all receive spirit.

lines.fa: یکی تیشه بگیرید پی حفره زندان
lines.en: Take up an axe and dig through the prison wall;

lines.fa: چو زندان بشکستید همه شاه و امیرید
lines.en: when you have broken the prison, you are all kings and princes.

tafsir: Rumi is not praising physical death here.
He means the death of the small, frightened self, the one that keeps us in prison.
Die to that, he says, and you receive spirit.
The Sufis called it dying before you die. What is broken is only the prison.

poems.name: Come to My Grave With a Drum

lines.fa: ز خاک من اگر گندم برآید
lines.en: If wheat grows from my dust,

lines.fa: از آن گر نان پزی مستی فزاید
lines.en: and you bake bread from it, drunkenness will grow.

lines.fa: میا بی‌دف به گور من برادر
lines.en: Do not come to my grave without a drum, brother;

lines.fa: که در بزم خدا غمگین نشاید
lines.en: sadness is not fitting at God's feast.

tafsir: Rumi imagines wheat growing from his grave, and the bread still full of his love.
Then he gives instructions for visitors: bring a daf, the frame drum.
To this day, on Shab-e Arus, his tomb in Konya is filled with music and turning.
His followers took him at his word.

poems.name: Time to Leave

lines.fa: ای عاشقان ای عاشقان هنگام کوچ است از جهان
lines.en: O lovers, O lovers, it is time to leave the world;

lines.fa: در گوش جانم می‌رسد طبل رحیل از آسمان
lines.en: the drum of departure reaches the ear of my soul from the sky.

lines.fa: نک ساربان برخاسته قطارها آراسته
lines.en: Look, the camel driver has risen and lined up the camels;

lines.fa: از ما حلالی خواسته چه خفته‌اید ای کاروان
lines.en: he has asked our pardon. Why are you sleeping, O caravan?

tafsir: Life here is a caravan, resting for a night on a long road.
Before dawn the drum sounds and the camel driver gets ready.
Travellers would ask each other's forgiveness before setting out.
Rumi wakes us gently: the journey is starting. Wake up, and travel well.

poems.name: That Is Our City

lines.fa: ما به فلک بوده‌ایم یار ملک بوده‌ایم
lines.en: We were in the heavens; we were companions of angels.

lines.fa: باز همان جا رویم جمله که آن شهر ماست
lines.en: We will all go back there, for that is our city.

lines.fa: آمد موج الست کشتی قالب ببست
lines.en: The wave of 'Am I not your Lord?' came and built the ship of the body;

lines.fa: باز چو کشتی شکست نوبت وصل و لقاست
lines.en: and when the ship breaks again, it is the hour of union and meeting.

tafsir: In the Quran, before creation, God asks the souls: am I not your Lord? And they answer: yes.
Rumi calls that moment a wave, and says it built the ship of our bodies.
One day the ship will break.
But for him that is not a shipwreck. It is the hour when the soul finally meets the one it answered.

poems.name: The Spring Inside Death

lines.fa: در عین مرگ چشمه آب حیات دید
lines.en: In the very heart of death he saw the spring of the water of life,

lines.fa: آن چشمه‌ای که مایه دیدار آمده
lines.en: the spring from which the meeting with the Beloved flows.

tafsir: The water of life, in Persian legend, is found in the Land of Darkness.
Rumi places it inside death itself.
Where we expect only an ending, the one who sees clearly finds a spring.
And that spring is the source of seeing the Beloved face to face.

poems.name: Do Not Count Him Dead

lines.fa: گفت کسی خواجه سنایی بمرد
lines.en: Someone said: Master Sanai has died.

lines.fa: مرگ چنین خواجه نه کاریست خرد
lines.en: The death of such a master is no small thing.

lines.fa: شد همگی جان مثل آفتاب
lines.en: He became all soul, like the sun;

lines.fa: جان شده را مرده نباید شمرد
lines.en: one who has become soul must not be counted dead.

tafsir: Sanai was a great Sufi poet who lived before Rumi, and whom Rumi loved.
When news of a death arrives, this is how Rumi answers it.
Sanai did not disappear. He became entirely soul, like sunlight.
On this Shab-e Arus, we could say the same of Rumi himself. Thank you for remembering him with us.

outro: Thank you for spending Rumi's wedding night with us.
